scope.target: Chrono Trigger US Rev0 headerless, logical playable PC 07
scope.coverage: Current character, party, save, runtime-record, progression, naming, graphics, menu, battle, Tech, item, equipment, and recruitment boundaries relevant to Project Epoch
scope.completeness_claim: Bounded current consolidation of the Project Epoch corrections represented by this versioned ledger, not a complete ROM, RAM, event, or engine map
scope.research_change: The map remains a bounded consolidation; its palette entry now incorporates one separately documented private supported-slot emulator replay without changing any PC 07 ownership conclusion
scope.payload_policy: Metadata, addresses, hashes, conclusions, and relative evidence references only; no ROM, save, state, trace, or extracted game bytes

canonical_rom.mapping: C0-FF HiROM address masked to file offset 000000-3FFFFF

expanded_scaffold.identity: Project Epoch inert 8 MiB ExHiROM structural scaffold
expanded_scaffold.status: structural exception only; no production allocation or payload

pc_record_schema.meaning: innate-element selector plus unmapped low flags
pc_record_schema.qualification: high nibble mapped; low nibble unresolved

pc_record_schema.meaning: PC progress flags; bits 0 and 4 mapped
secondary combatant effect or category flags

pc_record_schema.qualification: partially mapped; PC templates seed zero

pc_record_schema.meaning: permanent or equipment status and immunity groups 0-4
remaining EXP to next level, little-endian u16
remaining TP to next single Tech, little-endian u16
level-1 stat baselines in growth order: Power, Stamina, unused Speed, Hit, Evade, Magic, Magic Defense
equipment-adjusted live stats in record order: Power, Stamina, Speed, Magic, Hit, Evade, Magic Defense
context-derived tail; menu adjusted max HP view and battle element modifiers
unmapped tail byte; initial FF sentinel is not proof of free space
pc_record_schema.qualification: owner preserved; no durable source meaning proved

entries.title: Logical PC, save/editor, graphics-source, and empty-slot values are separate namespaces
entries.historical_comparison: Historical work sometimes treated numeric 07 as one shared eighth-character or Epoch identity.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Numeric equality creates no cross-namespace ownership or mapping.

evidence.statement: Canonical party, record, name, and graphics consumers assign different meanings to the same numeric values.
Save-editor tooling uses 80 as its empty-party sentinel; this is a tooling convention, not a canonical playable identity.

entries.pc07_consequence: Every consumer must resolve logical PC 07 in its own namespace.
entries.required_action: Keep explicit, context-specific adapters; never implement a global 07-to-06 or 07-to-Epoch substitution.

entries.title: Active-party bytes and joined-state bit
entries.historical_comparison: Raw party operation and event-opcode transport of 07 was sometimes treated as proof of a complete eighth PC.

locations.role: cached active-party IDs following the field registry

entries.vanilla_ownership: Three active slots plus a joined mask whose bit 0 is structurally available.

evidence.statement: The three active-party bytes are transported through current vanilla save and field paths.
CharPartyFlagTable maps logical ID 07 to joined bit 01, while the field object registry has entries only for IDs 00-06 and is immediately followed by cached active IDs.

entries.pc07_consequence: Transport and a joined bit exist, but downstream record, menu, graphics, battle, Tech, name, and persistence validity does not follow.
entries.required_action: Publish 07 only after all dependent adapters and duplicate-free roster validation pass.

entries.title: Seven PC records end before the Tech and compatibility block
entries.historical_comparison: Community maps and save editors labeled slot-relative 0430 as an eighth or Epoch character record.
entries.vanilla_ownership: 0430-047F belongs to the seven-PC Tech and compatibility domain, not Epoch and not an eighth PC.

evidence.statement: Exactly seven 0050-byte PC records occupy 0200-042F.
Current save/load controls restore the protected 0430-047F block byte-exactly to its live compatibility destination.

entries.pc07_consequence: Naive record 07 reads and writes Tech state as HP, MP, EXP, equipment, and stats.
entries.required_action: Preserve 0430-047F and store Project Epoch data in a separately versioned sidecar.

entries.title: 0480 is serialized vanilla state, not free eighth-record storage
entries.historical_comparison: Zero bytes at 0480 in one save were proposed as a candidate backing record.

locations.role: vanilla global SRAM metadata following the bounded sidecar candidate
eight five-byte save-copy descriptors; loader begins at the end

entries.vanilla_ownership: 0480 lies inside the serializer's first 05B0-byte region and the checksum covers the whole 0A00-byte slot.

evidence.statement: The native serializer includes 0480; zero-filled sample bytes do not prove free space.

entries.pc07_consequence: Using 0480 as an appended record could overwrite conditionally meaningful vanilla state.
entries.required_action: Do not read or write a Project Epoch character record at 0480.

entries.title: Bounded three-record global SRAM sidecar candidate
entries.historical_comparison: This replaces the old plan to append a record inside each vanilla slot.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Bounded global SRAM gap candidate; not yet approved as a production allocation.

evidence.statement: The 01E0-byte geometry fits three 00A0-byte records and is outside the three vanilla 0A00-byte slots.
Existing vanilla boot/load controls preserve the candidate region without installing a Project Epoch writer.

entries.pc07_consequence: A sidecar can preserve vanilla slot ownership while carrying Schala state, subject to lifecycle proof.
entries.required_action: Finish normal-save, load, erase, New Game+, power-cycle, timing, and atomicity proof before allocation approval.

entries.title: Natural record formula collides with the live compatibility block
entries.historical_comparison: Historical maps correctly observed the id-times-0050 formula but mislabeled its vanilla ID 07 destination as a valid record.

locations.role: live seven-PC Tech and compatibility block

entries.vanilla_ownership: The formula 7E2600 plus id times 0050 is real; direct ID 07 aliases compatibility state at 7E2830.

evidence.statement: Menu, battle-load, battle-commit, and reload paths use the natural record formula.
Existing canaries bound the candidate relocation in selected field, menu, battle, save, New Game+, and attract controls without approving it.

entries.pc07_consequence: Natural PC 07 becomes viable only after the entire 0050-byte compatibility owner moves and every lifecycle path follows it.
entries.required_action: Complete the remaining runtime matrix before publishing 7E2830 as Schala's live record.

entries.title: Vanilla seeds seven records and the attract path overruns seven-row growth sources
entries.historical_comparison: Bytes following the seven initialization records were treated as an incomplete eighth character.

locations.role: monolithic new-game seed including compatibility state

entries.vanilla_ownership: CC0230-CC027F is starting Tech and compatibility state; the attract initializer loops eight destinations while reading seven HP and MP rows.

evidence.statement: Vanilla has exactly seven initialization records and a 0280-byte monolithic seed.
The attract path's eighth destination reads beyond each seven-row HP and MP source block.

entries.pc07_consequence: Extending only a copy bound initializes Schala from unrelated adjacent data.
entries.required_action: Provide explicit Schala initialization and preserve the relocated compatibility owner in normal, reset, New Game+, and attract paths.

entries.title: Record stat order and growth-array stat order are different
entries.historical_comparison: Community documentation propagated one Magic-before-Hit ordering as though it governed every stat array.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Base/live record order is Power, Stamina, Speed, Magic, Hit, Evade, Magic Defense; growth/progression row order is Power, Stamina, Speed, Hit, Evade, Magic, Magic Defense.

evidence.statement: The complete 0050-byte record schema distinguishes the base/live order from the runtime-confirmed growth-array order.

entries.pc07_consequence: Reusing one ordering for both structures silently swaps Magic, Hit, and Evade semantics.
entries.required_action: Encode each structure with its own named field order and test it independently.

entries.title: HP, MP, stat, and TP families have different row counts and collide under raw ID 07
entries.historical_comparison: CC25C2 was called an eighth HP row and the zero stat row was sometimes treated as a complete eighth-character definition.

locations.role: seven HP-growth rows of eight bytes
seven MP-growth rows of eight bytes
eight stat-growth rows of seven bytes; row 7 is zero
seven TP-threshold rows of sixteen bytes

entries.vanilla_ownership: HP and MP have seven rows; stat growth has an eighth zero row; TP has seven rows. Adjacent tables own every raw fallthrough.

evidence.statement: Exact table boundaries and row counts are reconstructed from the canonical ROM.

entries.pc07_consequence: Raw row 07 aliases the next family for HP, MP, and TP; the zero stat row supplies no complete progression model.
entries.required_action: Relocate or adapt all four families and author Schala's data deliberately.

entries.title: Battle commits slot work records through the natural character-record formula
entries.historical_comparison: No isolated eighth-record write is available merely because battle transports logical ID 07.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Battle work is active-slot based, then commits 0050 bytes to 7E2600 plus logical ID times 0050.

evidence.statement: The commit formula sends direct ID 07 into the live compatibility block.

entries.pc07_consequence: A successful battle could corrupt Tech state even if Schala rendered and acted correctly.
entries.required_action: Use the natural commit only after relocation; otherwise install an ID-aware commit adapter.

entries.title: Seven-byte active-membership map and seven-ID reserve-XP bound
entries.historical_comparison: An external reconstruction mislabeled the reserve-XP routine; changing only its seven-character loop bound would still read adjacent WRAM.
entries.vanilla_ownership: The map initializes IDs 00-06 only; the reserve scan awards 75 percent XP to IDs 00-06 and stops before 07.

evidence.statement: Canonical span and instruction-site hashes pin both independent seven-character boundaries.

entries.pc07_consequence: Reserve Schala receives no XP, while direct active-map lookup reads unowned adjacent 7EB1C5.
entries.required_action: Add an explicit PC 07 active-membership resolver and a fail-closed reserve-XP adapter after sidecar and roster validation.

entries.title: Single-Tech and combo-learning state occupies the natural PC 07 record window
entries.historical_comparison: The first bytes of this block were initially edited as incomplete eighth-character record fields before the forum corrected them to Tech state.

locations.role: ten ordinary learned triple-Tech group bytes
five equipped-rock or rock-Tech flag bytes

entries.vanilla_ownership: Every byte through 285B is mapped live seven-PC Tech or equipped-rock state; later compatibility bytes remain partly mapped and protected.

evidence.statement: Counts, learned masks, fifteen dual groups, ten ordinary triple groups, five equipped-rock flags, and their computed consumers are reconstructed from canonical code.

entries.pc07_consequence: Appending an eighth counter, mask, or combo row overwrites the next live state family.
entries.required_action: Relocate the complete compatibility domain and create an expanded Schala learning namespace.

entries.title: Spekkio event 11C directly addresses seven-PC Tech arrays
entries.historical_comparison: Generic event transport of PC ID 07 does not remove hardcoded absolute Tech-state operands elsewhere in event scripts.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Twelve commands touch selected 2830-series counters and 2837-series masks.

evidence.statement: All 513 event pointers and 1511 absolute commands were scanned, isolating the exact 12-site set.
Existing volatile-WRAM translations reproduce the twelve operations in prepared vanilla profiles without installing a ROM event.

entries.pc07_consequence: Relocating compatibility state requires event-operand translation before Schala's natural record can occupy 7E2830.
entries.required_action: Recompress and install the pinned translation only with the complete relocation adapter set, then rerun lifecycle guards.

entries.title: The eighth six-byte field is Epoch-facing and dialogue entry 7 is null
entries.historical_comparison: Historical proposals reused or relocated the Epoch/name ranges for PC 07.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Name-entry arithmetic reaches Epoch at ID 07, while the dialogue PC-name pointer table has no valid PC 07 target.

evidence.statement: Both the live-field formula and null dialogue entry are reconstructed from canonical code.

entries.pc07_consequence: Routing Schala through vanilla ID 07 naming corrupts or aliases Epoch and still fails dialogue substitution.
entries.required_action: Give Schala independent live, dialogue, save, load, menu, and recruitment name adapters.

entries.title: Playable graphics families contain seven PC entries and occupied successors
entries.historical_comparison: The first successor entries and zero-looking tails were treated as expandable eighth-PC storage.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Direct index 07 reaches NPC, vehicle, palette, assembly, auxiliary, or sentinel data depending on the table.

evidence.statement: The graphics, assembly, animation, auxiliary, palette, and descriptor consumers each expose a seven-PC boundary and occupied successor.

entries.pc07_consequence: A raw logical ID is not a safe graphics-source index.
entries.required_action: Resolve PC 07 to named expanded assets separately in field, battle, menu, overworld, palette, and animation contexts.

entries.title: Historical PC 07 display reused an occupied NPC descriptor associated with Melchior
entries.historical_comparison: The old prototype changed the first NPC descriptor and redirected its NPC users, making PC 07 appear coherent by moving Melchior's graphics-source use elsewhere.
entries.vanilla_ownership: The descriptor is statically occupied NPC data; the Melchior identity and historical relocation are documented participant history, not proof that Melchior was a PC.

evidence.statement: E4F023-E4F027 is the first occupied five-byte NPC sprite descriptor.
The historical developers identified the displaced normal occupant as Melchior and redirected NPC users elsewhere.

entries.pc07_consequence: Reassigning graphics index 07 evicts an NPC resource even though the NPC is not a playable character.
entries.required_action: Leave E4F023 and every Melchior/NPC user unchanged; dispatch Schala to a separate expanded descriptor.

entries.title: The eighth animation word is a required end sentinel, not a new PC start
entries.historical_comparison: The apparent eighth boundary and four-byte selector stride were sometimes generalized into a fixed-record/free-entry interpretation.

locations.role: eight boundaries delimiting seven PC animation spans

entries.vanilla_ownership: Boundary 7 is the Magus-end/NPC-start sentinel; auxiliary index 07 is occupied. Entrypoint N begins at N times 4, but sequences can overlap and have variable length.

evidence.statement: Eight boundary words delimit exactly seven PC animation packages.
Primary and auxiliary entrypoints use a four-byte selection stride without implying fixed four-byte records.

entries.pc07_consequence: Appending over the sentinel corrupts Magus/NPC animation extent, and copied selector semantics may conflict.
entries.required_action: Relocate and resolve a complete Schala animation package with explicit primary/auxiliary compatibility.

entries.title: Palette loaders and overworld staging are separate fixed-capacity paths
entries.historical_comparison: A successful field sprite or copied palette was sometimes treated as covering all playable presentation contexts.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Field loading copies twelve character-specific colors; several readers force bank E4. Raw overworld ID 07 lands in palette or staging data.

evidence.statement: Five logical field reload paths contain ten 0018-byte shadow copies, and overworld consumers have independent ID formulas.

Two fresh pre-Continue/load runs and matched clean controls completed bounded four-direction and run movement; at the six accepted motion checkpoints the twelve-color canonical-ROM-derived Schala NPC-family provider renders through Lucca's supported field path, without establishing PC 07 or a full replacement palette.

entries.pc07_consequence: Field success cannot authorize battle, menu, portrait, or overworld palette/index reuse.
entries.required_action: Provide context-specific expanded-bank readers and dedicated overworld/palette data while preserving all vanilla owners.

entries.title: Seven walking-sprite records are followed by active party-exchange scratch
entries.historical_comparison: A historical PC 07 experiment reused the Gaspar/party-exchange display area as though it were an eighth persistent record.
entries.vanilla_ownership: 19C0 is an active scratch/display owner, not unused eighth-PC storage.

evidence.statement: The menu record geometry ends after seven persistent PC records and direct ID 07 reaches 19C0.
Historical developers described the visible collision as the Gaspar party-exchange area.

entries.pc07_consequence: Widening the seven-record loop overwrites a live presenter/caster record.
entries.required_action: Virtualize Schala into a deliberate display slot and preserve the party-exchange presenter.

entries.title: Seven full portraits, a special Epoch route, and a separate save-preview path
entries.historical_comparison: Eight selector bytes were interpreted as eight complete playable portraits, and supported-slot preview success was treated as broader portrait proof.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Only seven complete full faces and seven palette pointers exist; the following context is the special Epoch/name-entry route. Save preview is independent.

evidence.statement: The full portrait blob divides exactly into seven 36-tile faces and the normal palette table has seven words.
The supported clone proves only its separate small preview path.

entries.pc07_consequence: Raw ID 07 aliases existing face/Epoch contexts and does not identify an eighth full portrait.
entries.required_action: Resolve an original full face dynamically and implement a distinct sidecar-backed save preview while preserving Epoch naming.

entries.title: The element/type map ends at code, not an eighth row
entries.historical_comparison: The seven-byte boundary was correctly found after an attempted eighth-byte edit crashed the menu.
entries.vanilla_ownership: C2A2CD begins Menu_RebuildCharListScreen; it is not table storage.

evidence.statement: Canonical reconstruction confirms the seven-byte table and exact code boundary.

entries.pc07_consequence: Direct ID 07 reads an instruction byte as an element selector.
entries.required_action: Resolve Schala's deliberate icon at the consumer without extending the table in place.

entries.title: Seven Tech owners and fixed contiguous single/dual/triple groups
entries.historical_comparison: Raw PC 07 inherited the first dual-Tech rows after Magus, leading to the correct conclusion that whole Tech families must move.

locations.role: seven two-byte character Tech base/count entries

entries.vanilla_ownership: Seven owner rows are followed by dual requirements; combo builders assume fixed action ranges and group widths.

evidence.statement: The seven owner rows, 37 range boundaries, and fixed dual/triple builder assumptions are independently mapped.

entries.pc07_consequence: Inserting one owner or command row shifts live combo data and still leaves signed/direct consumers unchanged.
entries.required_action: Relocate owner/group metadata and bind Schala's singles, six dual groups, and two triple groups explicitly.

entries.title: Low player commands are full; high Project Epoch actions require adapters
entries.historical_comparison: Unused-looking numeric command IDs were treated as globally available without separating marker and animation-config namespaces.
entries.vanilla_ownership: The byte-wide queue transports high values, but signed checks and direct table indexes do not uniformly accept them; same-numbered animation-config rows are separate owners.

evidence.statement: The command census and transport path establish the occupied low range and every known high-ID edge.

entries.pc07_consequence: Seventeen Schala actions cannot fit the four low values 7C-7F and cannot safely inherit same-numbered table rows.
entries.required_action: Use the proposed 80-90 overlay only after every signed/direct consumer and package binding is explicit.

entries.title: Player-Tech package selectors are separate from action-command IDs
entries.historical_comparison: A high action ID and a same-numbered package selector can look interchangeable even though they are consumed by different tables and fixed-bank readers.

locations.role: complete canonical player package resolver and installer

entries.vanilla_ownership: Config byte 0 resolves package selectors through CD5EF0 and fixed bank CE; command 1E and auxiliary config bytes retain independent fixed-bank readers.

evidence.statement: The complete resolver span, all 128 canonical bank/root identities, nested-script edge, and auxiliary fixed-bank readers are pinned.
Selectors 80-8F remain an unbound Project Epoch policy namespace with no installed symbolic package source.

entries.pc07_consequence: Numeric equality between Schala action 80-90 and package selector 80-8F creates no mapping or payload ownership.
entries.required_action: Preserve the canonical 00-7F path, decide command-1E stream handling, and bind one proved high package deliberately before authoring a helper.

entries.title: Tech presentation and behavior tables have independent bounds
entries.historical_comparison: A visible eighth Tech list was treated as progress despite incomplete targeting, cost, property, effect, animation, learning, and persistence coverage.

locations.role: 124 eleven-byte per-character command records for IDs 00-7B
72 twelve-byte property records for IDs 00-47; ID 01 begins at CC214B
MP-cost alignment or null entry for ID 00
one-byte named player-Tech MP costs for IDs 01-47

entries.vanilla_ownership: Names, targets, properties, costs, effects, animations, and learning use distinct ranges and consumer assumptions.

evidence.statement: Current audits pin the names, target, per-character command, property, and MP-cost boundaries, including their ID-zero alignment rows; the effects root remains documented pending complete tracing.

entries.pc07_consequence: Making one list render does not make a Tech battle-valid, learnable, persistent, or uniquely owned.
entries.required_action: Resolve each table independently from named expanded descriptors and preserve each canonical table's exact existing range and owners.

entries.title: The seven basic-action IDs end at HP-growth data
entries.historical_comparison: CC258A was initially treated as PC 07's basic attack before the forum corrected it to HP-growth data.
entries.vanilla_ownership: The next byte at CC258A is the first HP-growth byte.

evidence.statement: Canonical reconstruction confirms both the seven-entry selector and adjacent HP table.

entries.pc07_consequence: Direct ID 07 selects HP-growth data as an action ID.
entries.required_action: Return Schala's action from named expanded data at the consumer; do not append a byte.

entries.title: The eight-byte approach-policy table already owns entry 07
entries.historical_comparison: A table containing eight bytes is not necessarily an unused eighth-PC row.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Entry 07 is an occupied FF value that takes the nonzero pathfind branch.

evidence.statement: The complete eight-byte table and consumer branch are pinned.
The Crono consumer route is observed in the current battle-action tranche.

entries.pc07_consequence: Raw ID 07 obtains an existing policy by accident, not a designed Schala attack approach.
entries.required_action: Preserve the eight occupied bytes and add an independent PC 07 resolver.

entries.title: Three adjacent seven-entry selector families alias one another
entries.historical_comparison: File 0D400E was labeled an eighth-character attack byte.
entries.vanilla_ownership: CD400E is both where raw PC 07 falls through from the second family and Crono's actual critical selector in the third family.

evidence.statement: The complete three-family boundary chain and all three consumers are pinned.
Crono's critical route reads the CD400E owner in the accepted battle-action trace.

entries.pc07_consequence: Patching 0D400E for Schala changes Crono's critical animation.
entries.required_action: Adapt all three consumers independently and leave every vanilla selector unchanged.

entries.title: Logical PC 07 has a structural equipment bit but not complete menu capacity
entries.historical_comparison: An available bit was sometimes treated as a complete eighth-character equipment implementation.
entries.vanilla_ownership: Item permission uses bit 01 for ID 07, while roster scans and menu buffers remain seven-PC bounded.

evidence.statement: The permission table and AND consumer expose a unique PC 07 bit.

entries.pc07_consequence: Schala-only masks are expressible, but general items, menu presentation, stats, weapon animation, and save behavior still need adapters.
entries.required_action: Assign item masks deliberately and runtime-test every equipment and stat-recalculation path.

entries.title: Candidate item IDs E8-EE are only unclaimed in audited location events
entries.historical_comparison: Unknown or apparently unused item IDs cannot be promoted to globally free storage from one table or event scan.
entries.vanilla_ownership: E8-EE are unclaimed by every canonical location-event script path audited, but global item ownership is not yet proved.

evidence.statement: All 513 location-event pointer entries and every valid referenced script contain no E8-EE item operand.

entries.pc07_consequence: Installing item records prematurely could collide with shops, inventory, battle, graphics, descriptions, or other classifiers.
entries.required_action: Finish the remaining global item adapters and allocate expanded descriptors before binding the IDs.

entries.title: Party operation 1 replaces slot 3 when the active party is full
entries.historical_comparison: Writing or adding ID 07 through the vanilla party operation was treated as a capacity-safe append.
entries.vanilla_ownership: The roster can represent eight recruited PCs, but operation 1 displaces active slot 3 into reserve when no active slot is open.

evidence.statement: The full-party Magus recruitment path proves reserve registration before naming and later active insertion.
Party operation 1's replacement behavior and roster geometry are mapped.

entries.pc07_consequence: A naïve Schala recruitment can silently replace an active character even though reserve capacity exists.
entries.required_action: Use an explicit open-slot helper and register Schala directly in reserve on the full-party branch.

entries.title: Historical Project Schala replaced Magus rather than adding a coexisting PC 07
entries.historical_comparison: Project Schala's visible Schala was sometimes discussed as though it proved a genuine eighth playable character.

locations.role: supported Magus graphics span used as a replacement reference

entries.vanilla_ownership: The prototype used Magus's supported record, equipment, element, Tech, save-preview, menu, and dialogue routes.

evidence.statement: The project author explicitly described Magus replacement and future rework for coexistence.
The graphics, palette, corrected assembly, and playable-animation boundaries are independently confirmed for supported-slot comparison.

entries.pc07_consequence: The project is a valuable PC 06 consumer checklist but supplies no natural-ID storage, capacity, save, or coexistence proof.
entries.required_action: Use it only as replacement-path comparison and independently implement every PC 07 namespace.

entries.title: Mirrored ExHiROM header map mode is structural metadata, not allocatable space
entries.historical_comparison: A one-byte historical change at file 40FFD5 made expanded pointers alias bank 01 instead of bank 41.

locations.role: mirrored ExHiROM map-mode byte in the inert 8 MiB scaffold

entries.vanilla_ownership: The byte belongs to the mirrored expanded header and controls mapping recognition.

evidence.statement: Historical debugger evidence observed the bank 41 to bank 01 alias after the bad value.
The current inert scaffold validates both headers, map mode, size, checksum, mirror, and fill invariants.

entries.pc07_consequence: Correct expanded pointers fail globally if the ROM is no longer recognized as ExHiROM.
entries.required_action: Treat both header copies as pinned structure and allocate only named expanded regions outside them.
